PASSO 1: Em português você diz «você» pa: STEP 1: In English you say «you» to almost everybody. In Russian there are two forms, and choosing the right one shows respect. STEP 2: Use «ты» (tih) with friends, family, young colleagues and children. With «ты», say «Привет!» (pree-VYET) and «Пока!» (pah-KAH). STEP 3: Use «вы» (vih) with strangers, bosses, teachers, older people, and in shops and offices. With «вы», say «Здравствуйте!» (ZDRAH-stvooy-tyeh) and «До свидания!» (dah svee-DAH-nee-yah). Tip: the first «в» in «Здравствуйте» is not pronounced. STEP 4: «вы» is also the plural: if you speak to two people, even friends, you say «вы». STEP 5: When in doubt, use «вы». Nobody is offended by too much respect, and the other person can suggest «ты». Como dizer o seu nome: «Меня зовут…»: How to say your name: «Меня зовут…»
PASSO 1: Para dizer o seu nome, o russo: STEP 1: To say your name, Russian literally says «me they call…». The ready-made sentence is «Меня зовут Лена» (mee-NYAH zah-VOOT LYEH-nah): «меня» is «me», «зовут» is «they call». Put your own name in place of «Лена». STEP 2: To ask a friend, say «Как тебя зовут?» (kahk tee-BYAH zah-VOOT). To ask someone who deserves respect, say «Как вас зовут?» (kahk vahs zah-VOOT). STEP 3: Notice: there is no word for «my», «is» or «am». The sentence is short and the name comes last, just as it is. STEP 4: After the name, the polite reply is «Очень приятно» (OH-cheen pree-YAHT-nah), «nice to meet you». The other person answers «Мне тоже» (mnyeh TOH-zheh), «me too». STEP 5: For now, learn «меня», «тебя» and «вас» as ready-made blocks. In lesson 14 you will see where these forms come from.

Os pronomes e a ausência do verbo «ser»: Pronouns and the missing verb «to be»
PASSO 1: Os pronomes são palavras curtas: STEP 1: Pronouns are short words, and you have already used three: «я» (yah), I; «ты» (tih), you (informal); and «вы» (vih), you (formal or plural). STEP 2: The others are «он» (ohn), he; «она» (ah-NAH), she; «оно» (ah-NOH), it, for neuter things; «мы» (mih), we; and «они» (ah-NEE), they. STEP 3: Russian has no verb «to be» in the present tense. To say «I am a student», say only «Я студент» (yah stoo-DYENT). Literally: «I student». STEP 4: This applies to all pronouns: «Он студент», «Она студентка», «Мы тут», «Они там». No verb in the middle. STEP 5: In writing, between two nouns, a dash is sometimes put in place of the «is»: «Антон — студент». When speaking, make a small pause where the dash is. STEP 6: A man says «студент» and a woman says «студентка». With «Я», the next word shows the gender of the speaker.
em português o verbo muda com a pessoa:: in English the verb changes with the person: «I am», «he is», «we are». In Russian, in the present tense, nothing changes and nothing appears: only the pronoun and the rest of the sentence.

O gênero dos substantivos: masculino, fe: The gender of nouns: masculine, feminine and neuter
PASSO 1: Todo substantivo russo tem um g: STEP 1: Every Russian noun has a gender: masculine, feminine or neuter. You find the gender by looking at the last letter. STEP 2: Ends in a consonant, or in «й»: masculine. Examples: «брат» (braht), «дом» (dohm), «город» (GOH-raht) and «музей» (moo-ZEY). STEP 3: Ends in «а»: feminine. Examples: «мама» (MAH-mah), «сестра» (sees-TRAH), «школа» (SHKOH-lah) and «жена» (zhee-NAH). STEP 4: Ends in «о»: neuter. Examples: «кино» (kee-NOH), «метро» (mee-TROH) and «фото» (FOH-tah). STEP 5: Careful: in English only people and some animals have a gender (he and she), while things are «it». In Russian every noun has one, so a thing can be «he» or «she»: «брат» is «он», «сестра» is «она», and «кино» is «оно». «Игра», game, is feminine in Russian. And «папа» is masculine, although it ends in «а», because he is a man. STEP 6: The gender chooses the pronoun: masculine is «он», feminine is «она» and neuter is «оно». That is why «брат» is «он», «сестра» is «она» and «кино» is «оно». You will see other endings in lessons 4 and 5.
